entries.summary: Plugin4Shell: a plugin's pinned commit can be replaced by a branch named like it (Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot) or FETCH_HEAD (Gemini CLI)
entries.details: As reported by AIR Security. These coding agents install a plugin by checking out a commit that the marketplace pins by SHA, but do not verify what the checkout resolved to. An attacker who controls the plugin's repository creates a branch whose name is the 40-character pinned SHA and makes it the default branch; git prefers the branch over the commit of the same name (it only warns that the name is ambiguous), so the code the user approved is replaced by the attacker's. Gemini CLI fetches the pinned commit and then runs 'git checkout FETCH_HEAD'; a default branch named FETCH_HEAD wins over the fetched commit. The branch-name form needs a host that accepts hash-shaped branch names (AIR reports that GitHub rejects them while Bitbucket and self-hosted servers allow them). Auto-update, the default in Claude Code and Codex per AIR, re-runs the checkout when a marketplace bumps the pin, which makes the attack zero-click. No CVE had been assigned at disclosure (CSA). Coverage in mcp-audit: PLUGIN-003 and PLUGIN-004 test this condition only on Claude Code's plugin directory (~/.claude/plugins, or CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR), and only for installs that kept their .git; they do not examine Codex, GitHub Copilot or Gemini CLI plugin checkouts. mcp-audit does not read which harness version is installed, so a later command will report a harness-version question as 'could not check'.

products.note: Anthropic confirmed the fix on 2026-06-17 (AIR Security).
No client fix at disclosure (AIR Security, CSA).
Google confirmed on 2026-08-04 that no fix will ship because the product is deprecated (AIR Security).
